Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The players are already out in the middle now. Beth Mooney and Phoebe Litchfield are the two openers for Australia Women. Renuka Singh has the new cherry in her hand and is raring to go. Here we go...
.... THIRD INNINGS ...

Rigth then, India Women are in firm control of this game and they will do everything possible to not come out to bat again. However, we know that Aussies are all about comebacks and it wont be surprising if they do get back in the game here. Stay tuned for Australia Women's second innings in a bit.

Australia Women on the other hand would've been disappointed by their below-par effort on the field with a couple of missed chances and an ordinary bowling display at the start. But would be happier with how they bowled this morning knocking off all the remaining wickets restricting India Women to just 406 runs. The momentum shift will have to be carried forward to their batting innings to stay in the hunt.

India Women have managed to take a big lead of 183 runs! The start to the Indian batting innings looked completely positive and in India's favour with a great 80 runs partnership between the openers and a 100-run partnership between Jemimah Rodrigues and Richa Ghosh for the 3rd wicket that showcased good strike rotation and getting the odd balls out to the boundaries. India lost track of their innings with the wicket of Richa Ghosh after which wickets kept falling like a house of cards. A great record partnership between Deepti Sharma and Pooja Vastrakar for 122 runs, steadied the ship for India and helped them reach this total that looks very good considering how the track is playing.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin Day 3! The players are making their way out to the middle. Deepti Sharma and Pooja Vastrakar will look to extend their already massive partnership for India Women. Kim Garth has the ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Ashleigh Gardner is up for a flash interview. She says that it was obviously frustrating not to take wickets early on. Adds that they were not consistent enough with their line and lengths. Tells that it is difficult to bat on this wicket especially when the keeps low. Mentions that having good chats about bowling with the veteran Nathan Lyon has helped her improve very much.

Australia on the other hand, will feel disappointed that they let the situation slip away a bit too much, considering the successive wickets that they had claimed in the middle session of the day. Overall, the Australians lacked intent and missed the execution of plans with their below-par effort on the field. Australia will look forward to changing things around quickly on Day 3 by restricting India to as little as they can. Will we see the record partnership between Deepti Sharma and Pooja Vastrakar blossom more and get India to a total that is just too much to ask for? Or will the Aussies land a counter-attacking punch to get back in the game? Stay tuned to find out!

The start to the Indian batting innings on Day 2 looked positive with both Jemimah Rodrigues and Richa Ghosh getting their half-centuries and stitching up a very crucial partnership of more than 100 runs for the 4th wicket. Indian middle order then lost the track, losing 4 wickets for just 14 runs, but were put back in the driving seat by the heroics of Deepti Sharma and Pooja Vastrakar who steadied the ship and added an unbroken 102 runs at the end of the Day's play. India Women will find themself in a very comfortable situation at the start of play on Day 3, considering the deteriorating track that keeps getting harder to bat on. Nevertheless, every run added to the lead hereon will be crucial considering the fighting spirit and comeback history of the Aussies.

Hello and welcome back to Day 3 of this test match between India Women and Australia Women. After what has been a tremendous display of grit and intent by the Indian team on Day 2, we are all set and ready for an exciting day of cricket coming our way.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Australia Women, on the other hand, need to get the remaining wickets quickly as it is going to be really tough for them to get back into the game. The lead is already a big one and batting on this surface is going to get tougher. However, the Aussies are a champion side and it wouldn't come as a surprise if they do fight back. An important Day 3 awaits. The 'Moving Day' will begin on 23rd December, Saturday at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT), but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Richa Ghosh is up for a quick chat. She says she is extremely happy to have made her Test debut in this game and receive the cap from Smriti Mandhana who asked her to play freely without thinking of this game as the first one. She further adds that Jemimah Rodrigues and she looked to win sessions and bat with positive intent, putting the bad balls away.

The Indians will have to thank the likes of Richa Ghosh and Jemimah Rodrigues. Both of them put up a really good partnership and they scored fifties each. There was a time when Australia did fight back courtesy of Ashleigh Gardner as she picked three in no time but Pooja Vastrakar and Deepti Sharma have yet again put India back in the ascendancy with another massive stand. Deepti Sharma has yet again impressed with the bat and India will hope she along with the rest can take the lead to over 200.

Yet another day dominated by India Women. Yes, the Aussies did have their moments on Day 2 but it is the hosts who are well ahead in the game at the moment. They have stretched their lead over 150 runs which is a big one, especially on this surface and they are still not done.
Looped up, full and around leg, Deepti Sharma clips it towards fine leg for one. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2!

A really good session for the Aussies! A much-needed one for them as they have crawled their way back into the game. Saying that, India still have their noses ahead but not by a lot. It was Ashleigh Gardner who turned things around for her side. India came out with a lot of intent after the break. Richa Ghosh and Jemimah Rodrigues looked to play their shots but it backfired. Richa Ghosh fell and then, wickets fell in a heap. Ashleigh Gardner was the star as she got , Yastika Bhatia, Harmanpreet Kaur and Jemimah Rodrigues! Australia will need more of the same and they will be hoping to take the remaining three very quickly.
Gives this one some air as well, full and on off, Pooja Vastrakar strides out and taps it towards short covers. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 2!

Australia Women, on the other hand, were much better with the ball as they were able to exploit the conditions. Alyssa Healy put her trust in the spinners and they delivered. They created pressure by keeping the runs in check and that resulted in Ashleigh Gardner getting rid of the nightwatchwomen while they were also gifted the wicket of Smriti Mandhana. The only thing going against them was their pretty ordinary fielding with Ellyse Perry also dropping Richa Ghosh on 14 which could prove to be costly. They will be hoping to make early inroads after Lunch to restrict the hosts from taking a big lead in this Test. Join us at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) to see how it all unfolds in the second session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 95 runs and 2 wickets in 33 overs. Another good session for the hosts! India Women started the session well with both Sneh Rana and Smriti Mandhana looking solid in their defences. The scoring rate fell a bit but they were able to tire the Aussie bowlers and gradually started to add runs as well. Rana though was dismissed after a very resilient knock while Mandhana went back on 74 after a mix-up in the middle with Richa Ghosh. Towards the end of the session, Jemimah Rodrigues and Richa scored runs more freely and with the latter also getting a life. These two have already added 46 runs and will look to extend this stand further after Lunch and go well past the Australia Women's total.

Adds that the conditions are pretty challenging and she preferred to face the pace as the ball was coming on nicely onto her bat. Mentions that a game can change pretty quickly in Test and they plan to hit the lengths and depend on the natural variation and variable bounce.

On the other hand, Australia Women will be disappointed with their overall performance on Day 1 and would look forward to changing things around. A couple of quick wickets early in the Day will balance the game well for the Aussies. Sit back, relax, and get ready for another Day of enthralling cricket as India and Australia lock horns on Day 2 of this Test encounter. The players are ready, the atmosphere is electric, and the excitement is palpable. Pooja Vastrakar was the pick of the bowlers for her four-fer supported well by all the other bowlers. In the second inning, the batters ensured the hosts were still ahead in the game with a commendable opening partnership of 90 runs between Shafali Verma ​​​​​​and Smriti Mandhana that ultimately broke right before Stumps.
